prompt: What is the context window of an LLM?
completion:
**Short answer**

The *context window* of a large language model (LLM) is the maximum number of tokens (pieces of text) that the model can “see” at once while producing a prediction. It is the length of the sliding window of input tokens that the transformer’s self‑attention mechanism can process in a single forward pass.

---

## 1. Why the context window matters

| Reason | What it affects |
|--------|-----------------|
| **Prompt size** | How much text you can feed into the model at the start of a generation. |
| **Conversation history** | In a chat, the model can only remember the last *N* tokens of the dialogue. |
| **Long‑form generation** | The model can keep the entire generated text in memory only up to the window size. |
| **Fine‑tuning & training** | During training, batches contain sequences that fit into the window. |
| **Model capacity** | Larger windows typically mean more computation and memory usage (quadratic cost in tokens). |

---

## 2. Tokens vs. characters vs. words

1. **Tokens** are the basic units the transformer works on.  
   - They are usually sub‑word pieces (e.g., WordPiece, BPE, SentencePiece).  
   - One token can be a single character, a word, or a common sub‑word.  
   - The average English token length is about 4–5 characters, so 2048 tokens ≈ 10 k characters.

2. **Why tokens matter for the window**  
   - The model’s architecture (self‑attention) is defined over a sequence of token embeddings.  
   - The window size is a hard architectural limit: you cannot feed more than *N* tokens to the model in one forward pass.

---

## 3. How the context window is defined

| Model | Base architecture | Context window |
|-------|-------------------|----------------|
| GPT‑3 (175 B) | Decoder‑only transformer | 2048 tokens |
| GPT‑3.5‑turbo | Decoder‑only transformer | 4096 tokens |
| GPT‑4 | Decoder‑only transformer | 8192 tokens (GPT‑4), 32 k tokens (GPT‑4‑32k) |
| LLaMA 2‑70B | Decoder‑only transformer | 4096 tokens |
| LLaMA 2‑70B‑Chat (with longer context) | Decoder‑only transformer | 8192 tokens (some variants) |
| Mixtral‑8×7B | Mixture‑of‑Experts + transformer | 8192 tokens (default) |
| Gemini Pro | Multimodal transformer | 8192 tokens |

*Note:* The numbers above are the *maximum* tokens the model can attend to. In practice, you rarely hit the hard limit because you often pad or truncate.

---

## 4. The mechanics inside a transformer

1. **Tokenization** → a list of token IDs.  
2. **Embedding** → each token ID becomes a vector.  
3. **Positional encoding** → adds position information.  
4. **Self‑attention** → each token attends to every other token in the window.  
   - Complexity: O(*N*² × *d*), where *N* is the window size and *d* is the hidden dimension.  
5. **Output** → next token probability distribution.

Because the attention matrix has size *N* × *N*, the model cannot process arbitrarily long sequences without changing the architecture or using approximations (e.g., sparse attention, memory‑augmented transformers).

---

## 5. Practical implications

| Use case | How the window affects you |
|----------|---------------------------|
| **Prompt engineering** | If you want to give the model a long background (e.g., a 15 k‑word article), you may need to truncate or summarize to fit within the window. |
| **Chatbots** | Only the last ~8 k tokens of the conversation are remembered. If you need to recall earlier parts, you must summarise them into a shorter “memory” prompt. |
| **Text generation** | When generating very long text (e.g., a novel), the model will “forget” earlier chapters once you exceed the window. Techniques such as *chunking*, *summarisation*, or *external memory* can help. |
| **Fine‑tuning** | Training data longer than the window must be broken into overlapping chunks; the model only sees one chunk at a time. |
| **Inference cost** | Doubling the window size roughly quadruples compute and memory usage. |

---

## 6. Extending or working around the window

| Technique | What it does | Typical trade‑offs |
|-----------|--------------|--------------------|
| **Chunking / sliding window** | Process text in overlapping blocks, then stitch outputs. | May lose long‑range coherence. |
| **Memory‑augmented transformers** (e.g., Reformer, Longformer, BigBird) | Sparse attention patterns reduce complexity. | Extra engineering; not all models support them. |
| **External summarisation** | Summarise older context into a short “memory” prompt. | Requires extra summarisation step. |
| **Multi‑pass inference** | Run the model multiple times, feeding it a shorter prompt each time and stitching outputs. | Increases latency. |
| **Hierarchical models** | Encode chunks separately, then combine embeddings. | Adds complexity. |
| **Prompt engineering** | Use short, precise prompts that include only essential context. | Requires skill. |

---

## 7. Quick “cheat‑sheet”

| Model | Max Tokens | Approx. Characters | Key use |
|-------|------------|--------------------|---------|
| GPT‑3 (175 B) | 2048 | ~10 k | General tasks, moderate prompts |
| GPT‑3.5‑turbo | 4096 | ~20 k | Chat, longer prompts |
| GPT‑4 | 8192 | ~40 k | Long‑form writing, code |
| GPT‑4‑32k | 32 k | ~160 k | Very long documents |
| LLaMA 2‑70B | 4096 | ~20 k | Research, custom fine‑tune |
| LLaMA 2‑70B‑Chat (8192) | 8192 | ~40 k | Conversational AI |
| Mixtral‑8×7B | 8192 | ~40 k | Multi‑modal, cost‑effective |
| Gemini Pro | 8192 | ~40 k | Text + image, generative AI |

---

## 8. Bottom line

The **context window** is the transformer’s *finite view* of the text. It determines how much of the prompt, conversation, or document the model can simultaneously attend to. Understanding this limit helps you design prompts, manage memory in conversations, and plan computational resources. If you exceed the window, you need to truncate, summarise, or employ special architectures that extend the effective window.
